claim: CGEL distinguishes rigid order from labile preferences among modifiers.
evidence_summary: A context that has already established the set of large sofas licenses black large sofa.
finding: A contextually reversed size/colour sequence fits the stated account.
inference: Is size-before-colour a rigid ordering constraint or a contextual preference?

evidence.passage: §15, p. 452. CGEL distinguishes rigid order from labile preferences among modifiers.
evidence.example: Suppose the large sofas are already established as a set and colour distinguishes two of them. Within that set, black can precede large in black large sofa. This is the sort of contextual reversal §15 anticipates.
evidence.establishes: A reversal in an appropriate context supports the description of a preference. It could refute only a rigid ordering rule.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
